newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 155-170 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 155-170 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 155-170 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 120 bcf to 185 bcf for the week ended January 31.
While there was little extreme weather last week, traders said views differed over how much pressure there was on storage operators, particularly in the East, to trim stocks.

"I think we're going to see some pretty strong withdrawals in coming weeks (regardless of weather). Pressure is building to get gas out right now," said one Texas trader, noting backwardated cash-to-futures spreads also encouraged stepped-up withdrawals.

Another Texas trader agreed. "The HDDs (heating degree days) would indicate a 151 bcf draw, but I added some additional b's (bcf) because storage operators have to get gas out to keep stocks in balance."
In last report, overall stocks fell by 150 bcf, in line with expectations, but eastern inventories were still 147 bcf, or 18 percent, above year-ago. The four week average drawdown is 139 bcf.
For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 213 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would move overall stocks back to about a 45 bcf surplus to 1996.

Eastern storage, which fell by 127 bcf in 1996, should remain at a significant surplus to year-ago, while producing stocks, which dropped by 54 bcf, and western stocks, which fell by 32 bcf, were likely to continue to significantly lag last year's levels, traders said.
